---
title: astroimred
subtitle: Read FITS files, combine exposures, and measure sources.
---

Start with the [FITS quickstart](quickstart.qmd), then follow the
[reduction learning path](tutorials/index.qmd). The examples start with
synthetic images before introducing observation files.

`astroimred` connects FITS file management, image reduction, and photometry
through Astropy `CCDData`. Array combination uses
[imcombiners](https://ysbach.github.io/imcombiners/); pixel-aperture geometry uses
[astroapers](https://ysbach.github.io/astroapers/).

::: {.task-links}
| Your task | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Read and inspect FITS files | [Quickstart](quickstart.qmd) |
| Apply bias, dark, and flat masters | [Calibration](tutorials/calibrate-images.qmd) |
| Combine calibrated exposures | [Image combination](tutorials/combine-images.qmd) |
| Process FITS files from a terminal | [Command-line tools](tutorials/command-line.qmd) |
| Find arguments and return values | [API reference](api/index.qmd) |
:::

Continue to [aperture photometry](tutorials/aperture-photometry.qmd) when
your images are ready for source measurements.

## Install

Use Python 3.11 or newer. Install the full extra for all examples on this site:

```bash
uv pip install "astroimred[full]"
```

```python
import astroimred as air
```

The API reference uses canonical module paths. Convenience imports such as
`air.load_ccd` and `air.fits_summary` remain useful for short scripts.
